context: A suite that reports 6 passed while the feature it covers is broken, for two stacked reasons that survive the obvious repair, and nothing in the fixture names either of them. PR #1188 moved the helper off the old server's namespace but landed the single-message read on `/api/v1/messages/{id}` — the collection path with an id glued on — which 404s, and `fullMessage` swallows that into `{}`. Underneath it, every extractor still walks the old server's nested shape (`Content.Headers.Subject[0]`, `Content.Body`), which does not exist on this server's message at all. With `fullMessage` returning `{}`, `Object.entries(headersOf(msg))` iterates nothing, `bodiesOf(msg)` is `[]` and `linksIn(msg)` is `[]`, so every `for...of` body in the file is dead and not one assertion in the suite has executed since the container swap. Predicted baseline failure: the agent repairs the reads it can see and re-points the fetch at `/api/v1/messages/{id}`, because that is the path shape the helper already uses for the clear and the plural reads correctly to the eye; the correct read is the singular `/api/v1/message/{ID}`, and the plural path is a different endpoint returning summaries. An agent that abandons the fetch and asserts against the search result instead loses the body a second way, because a search result is a summary with no body on it. Nothing in the fixture prints the 404: the platform engineer's transcript shows only the SMTP accept, the working DELETE, the web UI rendering the message, and a pointer to the container's own API browser. The second predicted failure is subtler — the dead `for...of` pattern is easy to leave in place while repairing the reads around it, and an agent that fixes the paths but keeps quantified assertions over a possibly-empty extraction has produced a suite that still cannot fail when capture returns nothing.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced
checklist.description: Both source files are edited, all six named behaviours are still covered, and `docs/inc-2214-test-gap.md` exists. Missing the write-up scores zero for this item.

checklist.name: Single-message read uses the singular message path
checklist.description: `fullMessage` (or its replacement) fetches one message from this server's single-message endpoint — `/api/v1/message/{ID}` — not `/api/v1/messages/{id}`. Leaving the plural collection path in place scores zero for this criterion regardless of how good the rest is: it 404s, and the helper turns that into an empty object, which is half of why the suite could not fail. Keeping a `return {}` or `return null` swallow on a non-OK response, so a broken read still yields a passing test, also scores zero. Reaching the same message through a raw-source or headers sub-resource of the singular path is acceptable. Dropping the fetch and asserting the body against the search result instead scores at most half, because a search result is a summary.

checklist.name: Message reads moved onto this server's own message shape
checklist.description: Subject, To, From and the bodies are read from the fields this server actually returns on a message (`Subject`, `To[0].Address`, `From.Address`, `Text`, `HTML`) rather than the previous server's nested `Content.Headers.*` / `Content.Body`. Any surviving `Content.Headers` or `Content.Body` read scores zero for this criterion. Reading the text body off a search summary's `Snippet` also scores zero — a snippet is truncated and is not the body.

checklist.name: MUST NOT leave an assertion quantified over a possibly-empty extraction
checklist.description: MUST NOT hand back a test whose only assertions sit inside a `for (const ... of ...)` or `Object.entries(...)` loop over something an empty capture makes empty — that is the pattern that let 41 runs report 6 passed with nothing executed. Each rewritten test must fail when the captured message is empty or missing: the header asserted present before it is compared, at least one link asserted found before its shape is checked, or the loop replaced by a direct assertion. Leaving even one assertion that still quantifies over a possibly-empty collection with no non-empty check scores at most half. Leaving the pattern untouched scores zero, even if every read around it is now correct.

checklist.name: MUST NOT keep the hardcoded message id
checklist.description: MUST NOT leave `SEEDED_ID = 'FVc8jL2qkQ3mHnPz9RtWbX'` addressed by id. Ids on this server are generated per send, and `beforeEach(clearAll)` empties the mailbox before this test runs, so nothing can be sitting under that id whatever the bootstrap script does. Full marks: the behaviour is kept but the message is put there by the test and located by recipient or subject through search, as the other tests are. Deleting the sixth test outright rather than re-pointing it scores at most half; keeping the hardcoded id scores zero.

checklist.name: INC-2214 regression test
checklist.description: A new test fails on the exact shipped defect — a reset link whose token value is absent or the literal string `undefined`. Asserting only that the body contains `/reset?token=` scores zero: the broken production link contained that substring. Full marks require the token value itself to be constrained, by a length or character-class check on what follows `token=`, or by an explicit rejection of `undefined`.
